subject: Plot Speed - ggplots vs googleVis vs rCharts

messages.author: ec79ef2df02af517
messages.subject: Plot Speed - ggplots vs googleVis vs rCharts
parts:
This post is really for general discussion, without any specific code problem for solving. Although I can provide example code if required.

I have built a shiny app, which loads a CSV of around 50MB and 213k rows. The Shiny app has in the region of 50 filters (sliders in the majority, but others too).

I've found that charting with ggplot2 is massively quicker than using either googlVis or rCharts. Now, I did expect to take a small speed hit, in the order of a couple of seconds perhaps, but the difference is much more than that.

Once I start plotting more than about 3k points, both the interactive libraries crawl to treacle slow. googleVis seems to be marginally quicker than the various rCharts options I've tried - Highcharts, xcharts and nvd3.

Using a 30k point line chart as a baseline, ggplot2 will have that static graphic made and displayed in Shiny within 2 seconds. Both googleVis and various rCharts options take between 15 and 30 seconds. My code is pretty straightforward, and to use googleVis as an example:

output$gchart <- renderGvis({

  gvisLineChart(plotdata(), xvar="DATE", yvar="Cumulative", options=list(width="1000", height="500"))

})

Nothing too tricky there.

From everything I've read, the real slow down seems to be parsing data our of Shiny via json to the javascript libraries.

My general discussion question is, do other people see the same slow down? Are there tips and tricks with either library to speed things up? Are their other faster interactive charting libraries worth investigating for use with Shiny?

Cheers
Phill
